record.original_question: Find the correct universal-algebra generalization of order congruence lattices and, more broadly, find examples of comodernistic lattices. In the source, an element m of a lattice L is left-modular when for every x ≤ y in L, (x ∨ m) ∧ y = x ∧ (m ∧ y), and a lattice is comodernistic when every nontrivial interval [a, b] has a coatom that is left-modular in that interval. Order congruence lattices O(P) of finite posets are given as examples, and the question asks whether a wider class of congruence lattices from universal algebra or similar settings yields comodernistic lattices.

evidence.quote: What is the correct universal algebra generalization of order congruence lattices?
More broadly: find examples of comodernistic lattices!
An element m of a lattice L is left-modular if for every pair x ≤ y of elements in L, we can write x ∨ m ∧ y without parentheses.
A lattice L is comodernistic if every nontrivial interval [a, b] of the lattice has a coatom that is left-modular in the interval.
The order congruence lattice O(P ) of a finite poset P consists of all the level sets of all the order preserving maps with domain P , ordered by refinement.
Perhaps there is a wider class of congruence lattices from universal algebra or similar which yields comodernistic lattices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a finite lattice with order relation $\le$, join $\vee$, and meet $\wedge$. An element $m\in L$ is called left-modular if for every pair $x\le y$ in $L$ one has
\[(x\vee m)\wedge y \;=\; x\vee(m\wedge y).\]
A nontrivial interval of $L$ is an interval $[a,b]=\{z\in L:a\le z\le b\}$ with $a<b$; a coatom of $[a,b]$ is an element $c\in[a,b]$ with $c<b$ and no element strictly between $c$ and $b$. The lattice $L$ is called comodernistic if every nontrivial interval $[a,b]$ of $L$ contains a coatom that is left-modular within the sublattice $[a,b]$.

For a finite poset $P$, the order congruence lattice $O(P)$ is the lattice of partitions of $P$ into nonempty convex pieces such that the natural quotient relation on $P$ is again a partial order, ordered by refinement; each such $O(P)$ is comodernistic.

(a) Identify a natural universal-algebra construction that generalizes the assignment $P\mapsto O(P)$ from finite posets to a wider class of algebras, in such a way that the order congruence lattices of finite posets arise as a special case and the resulting congruence-type lattices are comodernistic.

(b) More broadly, exhibit further families of comodernistic lattices arising from universal algebra or related settings.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution identifying a universal-algebra generalization of order congruence lattices that yields comodernistic lattices, nor a definitive list of new comodernistic-lattice families answering the broader question. Standard references on congruence lattices and modular/left-modular elements appear, but none explicitly settle this question, so the current status is unclear from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Congruence lattices of finite algebras (arXiv:1204.4305)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of representability of lattices as congruence lattices of finite algebras; does not address comodernistic property.
status_evidence.claim: General congruence-lattice literature does not record a known universal-algebra generalization of O(P) producing comodernistic lattices.

status_evidence.title: The Shape of Congruence Lattices (Kearnes–Kiss)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive monograph on congruence lattice shapes in universal algebra; no mention of comodernistic lattices.
status_evidence.claim: Authoritative universal-algebra reference contains no resolution of the comodernistic generalization question.
